steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (sniffs)

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (moves forward)

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (pats ground with hoof)

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: Moo!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: What is it? You find something?

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: Moo!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Caught someone's scent? Which way? Take me there.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: We notified everyone in advance, and got the surrounding areas evacuated in time. The homes I saw on the way were mostly cleared out too, so if someone was left behind, we got a problem.

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: Moo!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: This the spot? But there's nothing here.

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (nudges rubble with snout)

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Hey! Don't touch anything! Even if I can't see 'em, what if someone's down there?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Move aside, big one. I need to get past you.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Hello? Can you hear me?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I'm Brigid the nomad. If you can hear me and still move, then try to tap something hard like I'm doing.
There is a prolonged silence. Brigid starts to think her burdenbeast might have be mistaken. She looks around and sees the collapsed houses nearby, as well as the scattered supply packages.
It's been at least twenty-four hours since the Catastrophe. Finding any more survivors at this point is very unlikely.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Okay... no survivor then. Don't worry, big one, everyone makes mistakes.

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (stomps angrily)

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I know, I know! But I don't hear anything? Do you? Maybe you're smelling something else.

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: Moo!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Wait...
(lightly taps a stone brick)
(muffled voice)

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: ...There IS someone down there!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I'm here! I'm here! Talk to me. Do you have any light? Are you alone? Or—
—daughter—
Brigid crouches down, pressing her ear to the stone, where the sound is clearer. She leans in close, trying hard to hear every syllable.

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: Help...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I need you to speak clearer!

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: Help... my daughter...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Your daughter? So two of you down there, huh? How's your daughter doing? She there with you?
After a series of faint sounds, the woman's voice becomes clearer.

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: It's dark down here. I can't see much... We're buried. She fainted. I don't know...

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: I beg you, save us—

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Is your daughter near you?

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: Yes, yes... She's here in my arms. We're trapped under the rocks—

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: You're holding her? Take a deep breath, then listen to her closely. See if you can tell if she's breathing, or if she feels warm.

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: ...ughh... Yes, yes!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Good. From here on out, you have to keep talking to me.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: When people relax all of a sudden, they can quickly lose consciousness, so you need to keep talking to me, slowly.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: About anything. Just.. tell me how old your daughter is, the color of your hair, whatever.
The nomad nimbly gets up from the ground, removes her bells, raises them, and steps toward a more open area.
Amidst the sound of the bells and wind, she sends a distress signal to her fellow nomads in the wilds.

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: ...My daughter is 3-years-old. I have red hair...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: What race are you? I'm a Perro.

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: Feline... My daughter and I are both Felines...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: What's your name?

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: My name is Evelyn...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: What's your daughter's name?

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: What's that? I can't hear you.

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: Nomad? Nomad? Are you still there?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I'm here. I'm sending out a distress signal for my buddies. You're brave. You've kept her safe. Now we just have to wait for my friends to get here, and you're as good as rescued.

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: What? We still have to wait?

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: No... no... there's no time....

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Don't worry, there's time. You're still with me. Your daughter's still alive, right in your arms. We've confirmed your location, and there are no signs of aftershocks. You're going to be rescued. Trust me!

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: But I—I can't feel my legs. Even if you get me out, I'll be a cripple!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Wha—

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: So don't worry about me, or your companions. I beg you, nomad, just save my daughter!

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: I'm begging you!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Even without legs, you'd still have your eyes and your arms.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: You'd still able to see and touch. You protected your daughter from the Catastrophe, and now you want to leave her all alone?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: You don't get it, nomad. You don't understand...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Maybe I don't. So explain it to me. Remember what I said? Keep talking.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: But slowly. No more yelling like before. You'll just tire yourself out before you know it.

steps.name: Woman's Voice
steps.text: No...
...Brigid?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Nemos! Did you get my message? That was fast!

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: What message?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I taught you how to listen to the wind before, remember?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Of course you do. How else would you find me here? But that's not important. You're just in time. Over here, quickly.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Our mission is urgent, Wakewoman. We can't afford to waste any time.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I know, it's okay. This is my friend. She's a Taran nomad.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Nemos, who are those soldiers with you...?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: The Dublinn rescue team. We're here from Na Saoirsí.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: So it's a rescue mission, right? The people on that wee nomadic city made it out safe, but some of the others didn't. I found two survivors here.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Right here, under this rubble?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Yeah, right where I was standing. A mum and her kid. The mum's still conscious and talking, and the daughter's alive, but unconscious.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: So I take it you'll keep searching elsewhere?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Yeah. I already sent a message for my companions in the area. It's always faster working together, then we can move on right quick and keep looking for more.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Well, we're here now. You can go continue your search. Dublinn will take it from here.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Wakewoman, the mission The Brigadier gave us was to—

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I know, but there are two Taran survivors down there, and last I checked Dublinn was a Taran movement. Am I wrong?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: We'll take over the rescue mission here. Does that work for you, Brigid?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Of course. This isn't the first time we've worked together like this, it's not like you need me with all those extra hands.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Follow me. I'll show you the exact spot.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: ...We can split our forces. Some of you will stay here to handle the rescue, while the rest can come with me.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Wakewoman.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: You sound worried. How are the mother and daughter doing?

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: The nomad gave a good summary of the situation before the nomad left, but even with all of us working together, it'd take a while to clear the rubble and give them some breathing room before we can rescue them.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Our main task is to save the refugees who've been encircled by the Victorians, and we can't put that off for long.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: And we can't afford to split up either, or it'll take even longer.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Exactly. Also, the mother insists on speaking with you. She says she wants to talk to the person in charge.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Then let me speak with her.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Hmm... Haven't we already been through here? Isn't this where we discovered the mum and her daughter?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Looks like Nemos and the others have left, so they must've been freed a while ago. You sure your nose is working, big one? We overfeed you or something?

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: Moo, moomoo—

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (charges forward)

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: *sighs* Where you off to now? I was only kidding, okay? Don't run off!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Uh...
The rubble conceals the body buried deep beneath. It isn't until she gets closer that Brigid notices a hint of bright red on the gray surface, covered in dust and dirt.
The hint of red is actually a few locks of hair—a woman's hair.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: ...Evelyn?

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: (weak breathing)

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: She's still breathing... Hey, Evelyn! Wake up!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Evelyn!

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: *Cough* *Cough* Ugh...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: You're Evelyn, aren't you? Why'd they leave you behind?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: ...Where's Nemos and the Dublinn soldiers? They were supposed to rescue you—

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: Ma'am...

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: ...Rescue my daughter... Take her away from here...

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: I beg you...

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: Don't give up on her, and don't come back for me... Just take her!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: I already... told you... before.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: What did you tell me? I don't know. You'll need to say it again.
The nomad begins digging through the rubble with her tools. But working alone, her progress is too slow, and the woman's voice grows ever fainter.

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: These stones... I'm sure I'm... Infected...

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: Even if I survive... no one... will take me in...

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: ...And my legs... I can't move them...

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: I'll just be a burden.

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: Hrrh...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: No, no, no! You're wrong!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: You've got it all wrong!

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: Ma'am, please... Keep your distance, please...
'I'll rescue you.' 'I can still save you.' What should she tell her?

Any of those would be a lie. Brigid soon discovers that the rubble has already shifted from the previous rescue efforts. The broken bricks caught around the woman's waist are both supporting her and slowly killing her.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: ....'It's always faster working together.' And the fastest way was—

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: They split open the bricks above your head, removing the connection holding both sides together. All the broken bricks and rubble, all that weight, came tumblin' down right on top of you.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: They did it because they knew you'd protect your child. They knew you'd hold out, at least until she was safely out of your arms.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Right?
Ironically, rescuing the child had directly led to abandoning the mother. Even had they come back for her, they would not have been able to free her.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: But Nemos... How could she have let them do this?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I know they could've rescued both, if only they'd spent more time on it.

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (wailing)

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: *cough* *cough cough* Don't waste your energy, ma'am.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: ...I—you—

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Need anything else?

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: Yes. I heard them call you Wakewoman...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: You mean Nemos? I'm not Nemos, or a wakewoman.

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: ...I can't tell if you're real or not... but...

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: Can you wait... until I take my last breath... and...

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: ...bury me properly... as a wakewoman...?

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: Ngh... *cough*...
The woman can barely speak. Her chest heaves like torn bellows, rapidly but to no effect.
It is evident that her time is almost up.

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: *cough*
The woman furrows her brow, and her ashen face suddenly flushes red with pain.

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: Ugh...
The nomad stops her useless digging. She places her dirty palm on the woman's tense, wrinkled forehead.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: ...How's this? I've seen Nemos, er, the wakewoman do this before.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: A gentle touch can take away the pain and soothe the sick. Comfort parents who've lost their kids.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: But with the hands of a nomad...?

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (nudges Brigid with snout)

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Go cozy on up to her, big one. Maybe a wee bit of warmth will help.

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: ...Wakewoman? Ava... did you take Ava with you? My daughter...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: She's safe now. You can relax. Don't talk.

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: Ah—Ahh... thank you. Thank you so much.

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: *cough* *cough* You're still here. I want to...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: I want to see Na Saoirsí...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Na Saoirsí? Okay, I'll remember that.

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: Ugh... Argh!

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: It hurts... it hurts so much...! B—but... my legs are already numb... why——

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: Agh——*cough* *cough cough*!

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: Moo!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Don't talk anymore.

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: ...Grkh...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Go to sleep, Evelyn.

steps.name: Evelyn
steps.text: *cough*...ahh...

The woman takes a final, heavy breath. Her torso, which is sticking up from the ground, goes limp. Brigid suddenly realizes the woman's body must have been crushed in half by the stones some time ago.

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: Moo!

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (nudges Brigid hard with snout)

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I know, buddy. We need to get her out of there. Can't let her end up in a tuskbeast's belly.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Come here. Lend me a hand, err... paw.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Let's take her to see Na Saoirsí.
The Dark Woods allow the nomad passage. One nomad and one burdenbeast, carrying the departed to the edge of the forest.
Further along, at the end of the road, stands the bright city of Na Saoirsí, built of bricks and stones.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: *Huff*...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Sorry, Evelyn, I couldn't make a big enough bonfire. I can't return the fire to you like the wakemen do, like you wanted.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Also, I don't think you were infected? The Infected usually explode after death, but even after waiting for nightfall, nothing happened to you.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: But even if were, you shouldn't have died like that.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: On the way here, I thought about taking you to the ruins, to see the real wakemen, but you said you wanted to see Na Saoirsí.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: So after giving it some thought, I took you here.

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (soft wailing)

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Look on the bright side? Maybe...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Maybe Ava's already back in Na Saoirsí with Nemos by now. And if I bury you here, you won't get in anyone's way, but you can still see them from here. Maybe even... hear them.

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (brings some wildflowers and places them in front of the grave)

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Thanks buddy, but could you get me some flowers like these—

spans.text: Thanks buddy, but could you get me some flowers like

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Ah, forget, I'll get 'em myself. You stay here with Evelyn.
Brigid leaves the Dark Woods and ventures out into the open plains.
Here, the sound of the wind will no longer be disrupted by the rustling leaves. She will be able to clearly convey her words to her friend.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Wayward wakewoman, if you can still hear me...

a.text: The pledge you once made with your heart's flame, is it still in effect?
If it is, then why do you abandon those who can be saved?
If not, then why do you make such empty promises?
I am full of anger and doubt. I hope you'll come see me.
So that, under cover of darkness, with the Dark Woods as my witness,
I will see whether you still walk alongside me, from a thousand miles away.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: ...And now to pick a few flowers.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: She should be here by the time I get these flowers and weeds twisted into knots. Just like before, she'll climb over the ruined stone walls and cross the cape where the lighthouse went dark... to see me.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: She'll be here before sunrise.
There are two small bundles of nondescript flowers, one wrapped in leaves and placed in front of Evelyn's tiny grave, the other tied into a knot and placed at the nomad's feet.
She waits until dawn, just to dispel her lingering doubts. However, by the time the sun rises, all the questions she wanted to ask have lost their meaning.
She can wait no longer.

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (gently nudges Brigid with snout)

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: She didn't come.

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (gentle rub)

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Do you think she's always made this choice, every time, and I just never knew?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: She was always a wee different from the other wakemen. But ever since she left the ruins and the wilds, and went to the cities on the wheels...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: She hasn't been the same.

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: Moo, moomoo—

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I know, big one. It's past sunrise. She's not coming.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Okay, let's go! We've waited long enough.
Brigid stands up with the help of the burdenbeast. She leaves the knot where it is. Her limbs are a bit stiff, both from sitting too long and the bitter cold.
She takes one last glance at the burial mound in front of her, ignoring the sun-drenched nomadic city behind her.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Goodbye, Evelyn.
Quite a long while after the nomad leaves, another pair of hands picks up the withered, yellow knot on the ground.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Brigid?
